output.brief: Analyzer B's potassium results look sound. The single Level 2 QC miss is most likely a chance outlier or a one-off sampling glitch. Your own plan expects one or two such flags a month, and the repeat from the same vial passed. Other checks are consistent with this. Level 1, Level 3, sodium and chloride were fine. Level 2 averages are unchanged after the lot change. Re-running 43 patient samples on Analyzer A agreed with B within 0.1 mmol/L. B's patient median is stable. QC was run on time on all three days, so the staffing worry is not supported. Ward 6's high results are split evenly between Analyzers A and B. Most were delayed more than 3 hours in transit because the tube station is out of service, and the ward also took renal overflow patients. Both of those fit the high results better than an analyzer fault. I'd sign off: return B to potassium service, close the review without recall or lot quarantine, and refuse to widen the limits. Add extra Level 2 QC checks for a week. Don't record a sampling glitch as the confirmed cause, because nobody can show that. Ask Ward 6 to send repeat samples and get the tube station fixed. I'm fairly confident, but not certain, about the one-off cause.
